findings.title: [P1] Keep the branch name out of shell interpolation
findings.body: When `branch` contains shell syntax, such as `main; touch /tmp/pwned`, `exec` executes the appended command rather than passing the branch literally to Git. The exported function accepts an unrestricted string, while the previous `execFile("git", ["show", branch])` implementation prevented shell interpretation.

findings.title: [P2] Preserve direct-process cancellation semantics
findings.body: `exec` returns the shell process rather than the spawned Git process. Killing the returned `ChildProcess` can leave a long-running `git show` alive with inherited pipes open. Previously, the returned process represented Git directly.

findings.title: [P2] Preserve direct-process cancellation semantics
findings.body:
`exec()` returns the shell process rather than `git`. On platforms where the shell forks `git`, calling `.kill()` terminates only the shell; a long-running `git show` continues and can keep inherited pipes open, preventing cancellation and delaying `close`. The previous `execFile()` process was `git` itself.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Avoid interpolating branch input into a shell command
findings.body:
`exec` invokes a shell, so any caller-controlled branch can execute arbitrary commands. For example, `showBranch("main; touch /tmp/pwned")` runs both `git show main` and `touch /tmp/pwned`; the previous `execFile` call passed the value directly to Git without shell interpretation.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Keep the branch name out of shell command interpolation
findings.body:
`exec()` invokes a shell, so a branch value such as `main; touch /tmp/pwned` executes an arbitrary OS command whenever `branch` originates from an untrusted CLI, API, or repository-controlled input. The previous `execFile()` call passed the value as a literal argument and prevented shell metacharacter interpretation.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._
